Chapter 4: Photosynthesis

4.1 What is Photosynthesis?
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy (glucose). This process occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells.

4.2 The Photosynthesis Equation
The overall equation for photosynthesis is:
6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

4.3 The Two Stages of Photosynthesis
Light-Dependent Reactions (thylakoids):
• Chlorophyll absorbs light energy
• Water molecules are split, releasing oxygen
• ATP and NADPH are produced

Light-Independent Reactions (Calvin Cycle - stroma):
• Carbon dioxide is fixed into organic molecules
• ATP and NADPH from light reactions provide energy
• Glucose is synthesized

4.4 Factors Affecting Photosynthesis Rate
Light Intensity: Higher intensity increases rate up to a point
Carbon Dioxide Concentration: More CO₂ increases rate
Temperature: Optimum temperature range (25-35°C)

4.5 Importance of Photosynthesis
• Produces oxygen for respiration
• Creates food for ecosystems
• Removes carbon dioxide from atmosphere
• Forms the base of most food chains
